title: Career Roadmap · Agri Extension Assistant
summary: An Agri Extension Assistant helps farmers adopt improved agricultural practices through field demonstrations, crop advisories, training sessions, government-scheme awareness and links to agricultural experts.

about.label: Education
about.text: Agriculture / Horticulture diploma or degree, depending on the position

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Agriculture or Science with Biology, where available.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Biology, chemistry, agriculture, soil science and basic mathematics.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Requirements vary by diploma, degree and recruitment notification.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Crop production, irrigation, pest management, soil health and farmer education.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Communication, field observation, recordkeeping, teamwork and digital literacy.

items.text: Diploma in Agriculture → Field support, farmer outreach and eligible assistant positions.
Diploma in Horticulture → Fruit, vegetable, nursery and horticulture extension support.
B.Sc. Agriculture → Broader agricultural extension, advisory and technical opportunities.
B.Sc. Horticulture → Horticulture advisory, production and extension roles.
M.Sc. Agricultural Extension Education → Advanced extension, training, research and programme-planning opportunities.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: The title Agri Extension Assistant is not a single uniform qualification category. Government positions may require a specified diploma or degree, particular subjects, age limits and a recruitment examination. Verify the exact official notification.

ICAR

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Crop science, soil health, agricultural communication and field records.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Farmer advisory methods, field demonstrations, pest-management awareness and irrigation practices.

blocks.label: Year 3, if applicable
blocks.text: Digital extension tools, programme monitoring, farm visits and supervised fieldwork.

blocks.label: Final stage
blocks.text: Prepare farmer-training materials, complete a field project and apply for eligible roles.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Farmer crop-problem survey • Demonstration-plot report • Seasonal crop advisory leaflet • Farmer training attendance and outcome tracker.

blocks.label: Government / research
blocks.text: Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), agricultural universities, ICAR extension centres and state agriculture departments.

blocks.label: Private
blocks.text: Seed and fertiliser companies, agri-tech startups, farmer-producer organisations and agricultural NGOs.

blocks.label: Ideal exposure
blocks.text: Farmer meetings, crop demonstrations, pest-awareness campaigns, soil-health education and agricultural scheme communication.
KVKs provide farmer training, technology demonstrations and agricultural advisory support. Internship availability depends on the centre and programme.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic transcripts, subject prerequisites, English proficiency where required, funding evidence and student-visa documentation. Credit transfer depends on the university and programme.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: Agricultural Extension Assistant, Field Technician, Crop Advisory Assistant, Agricultural Outreach Worker.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Commercial agriculture, agricultural consulting, agri-tech, research and rural development.
International roles may require local agricultural knowledge, communication skills and relevant experience. Employment and visa sponsorship are not guaranteed.

Agriculture Student ↓ Field Trainee ↓ Agri Extension Assistant ↓ Experienced Field Executive ↓ Senior Extension / Technical Coordinator ↓ Agricultural Programme Manager ↓ Extension Specialist / Agribusiness Consultant
